scenes.headline: How one scale factor sizes every Gaussian
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Graticule! Today: how one number per scene lets one splatting model size its Gaussians on a teacup and on a city block.

scenes.text: Divide each scene by the median gap between neighbouring Gaussians, so the scale head always predicts against the same reference.
scenes.say: Take the median gap between neighbouring Gaussians and divide the scene by it. Now every scene asks the same question.

scenes.title: Gaussian spacing
scenes.say: Each pixel becomes one Gaussian. Neighbours land this far apart.

parts.note: how far the pixel's point is
parts.say: Further away, the points spread out.
A wider lens or a smaller image also spreads them out.

left.title: Radial normalization
items: Divide by mean distance to the camera
Spacing still moves with resolution and lens
left.say: The usual way divides by the mean distance to the camera. The gap between Gaussians still moves with resolution and lens.

right.title: Gaussian spacing normalization
items: Divide by median depth over focal length
Median spacing is pinned, by construction
right.say: SplatAnything divides by the median of depth over focal length. The typical gap is pinned.

steps.say: A frozen geometry model predicts depth and cameras.
One factor per scene rescales depth and camera positions so the median spacing hits a fixed target.
A Gaussian head predicts scale, opacity and colour per pixel. Centres stay where the depth put them.
Overlapping views merge per voxel, and a voxel is always about the same number of spacings wide.

scenes.title: Spread of median spacing across six toy scenes
scenes.note: synthetic scenes; the paper measures 4.5x on real data
scenes.say: On six synthetic scenes, the usual normalization leaves median spacing varying more than threefold. The new one pins it.

steps.say: In radial space, a street and a bedroom match in size, but their spacing differs, so the targets disagree.
In spacing space, the gaps match, and the same patch asks for the same Gaussian.

scenes.label: lower perceptual error than radial normalization, same model and training
scenes.say: In the paper's controlled ablation, that is worth three to thirteen percent on perceptual error.

scenes.text: Normalize by the quantity the head predicts against: depth over focal length, not distance from the camera.
scenes.say: Normalize by what the head actually predicts against. For splats, that is depth over focal length.

recap: Spacing is depth over focal length
Divide each scene by its median spacing
Same scale targets in every scene
scenes.say: Spacing is depth over focal length. Divide by its median. Every scene, same targets.
